issues.title: Late-assessment-cancellation window: 10 business days (Program Rules) vs 10 calendar days (Assessments Policy + Fees page)
issues.conservativePlanning: 10 business days (do not book/cancel any closer than 10 business days from the assessment date; $1,595 late-cancellation fee position)

sources.label: Program Rules Rule 10 (authoritative rules doc)
sources.anchorNote: approximate line anchor: pdftotext extraction, lines counted with text.split('\n') (1-indexed); treat as ±20 (clause-index convention)
sources.quote: If an assessment is cancelled and/or rescheduled within ten (10) business days of the Assessment Date, or the virtual/remote component of the assessment is cancelled and/or rescheduled within two (2) business days of the scheduled time for the virtual/remote component, then the full cost of one (1) assessment plus any travel expenses incurred to that point in time, will be paid by and invoiced to the Pharmacy

sources.label: Program Rules Rule 36 fee table (repeats 10 business days)
sources.anchorNote: approximate line anchor: pdftotext extraction, lines counted with text.split('\n') (1-indexed); treat as ±20 (clause-index convention)
sources.quote: Assessment Cancellation Fee incurred if assessment is cancelled within 10 business days of assessment date or failure to complete virtual/remote component of assessment [Rule 10]

sources.label: Assessments Policy 2.1 (policy doc)
sources.anchorNote: approximate line anchor: pdftotext extraction, lines counted with text.split('\n') (1-indexed); treat as ±20 (clause-index convention)
sources.quote: 2.1 Cancellation or changes less than 10 calendar days — Should an assessment date booking be changed or cancelled by a pharmacy owner or authorised delegate ... a cancellation fee equivalent to the current assessment fee (see schedule of fees), will be charged

sources.label: QSPP website Fees page (hub scrape)
sources.anchorNote: approximate line anchor: pdftotext extraction, lines counted with text.split('\n') (1-indexed); treat as ±20 (clause-index convention)
sources.quote: Fee Schedule as at 1 October 2026 ... Replacement assessment (late cancellation) $1,595 ... If you cancel a scheduled on-site assessment within 10 calendar days of the scheduled date, you will automatically incur...

issues.conflict: Rule 10 (business days) and Rule 36 (business days) vs Assessments Policy 2.1 + Fees page (calendar days). Rules and policy disagree on the unit.
issues.resolutionHint: Ask QSPP (support@qspp.com / interpretations@qspp.com) which unit is authoritative; meanwhile plan to the stricter window (10 business days). Agreement order places Program Rules above policies, which supports the business-days reading.

issues.title: Mid-Cycle Review scheduling window: four different statements
issues.conservativePlanning: months 15-21 within year 2 (align with Rule 8 + T&C definition; hub approximative)

sources.label: Program Rules Rule 8 (operative rule)
sources.anchorNote: approximate line anchor: pdftotext extraction, lines counted with text.split('\n') (1-indexed); treat as ±20 (clause-index convention)
sources.quote: A Mid-Cycle Review will be undertaken as a remote assessment to check-in and assess ongoing compliance with the program. This assessment is to be scheduled within the second year of the accreditation cycle (month 15 - month 21 of the 36-month accreditation cycle).

sources.label: Program Rules definitions table (same document)
sources.anchorNote: approximate line anchor: pdftotext extraction, lines counted with text.split('\n') (1-indexed); treat as ±20 (clause-index convention)
sources.quote: Mid-Cycle Review — A virtual review conducted remotely between months 13 and 24 of the 36-month accreditation cycle to assess ongoing compliance.

sources.label: Terms & Conditions definitions
sources.anchorNote: approximate line anchor: pdftotext extraction, lines counted with text.split('\n') (1-indexed); treat as ±20 (clause-index convention)
sources.quote: Mid-cycle Review — A virtual review conducted between months 15 and 21 of the 36-month accreditation cycle to assess ongoing compliance.

sources.label: QSPP website (hub scrape)
sources.anchorNote: approximate line anchor: pdftotext extraction, lines counted with text.split('\n') (1-indexed); treat as ±20 (clause-index convention)
sources.quote: One Onsite Accreditation Assessment every three years / One Mid-cycle Review approximately 18 months after the Onsite Assessment

issues.conflict: Rule 8 says months 15-21; the Rules’ own definitions table says months 13-24; T&C definition says months 15-21; hub page says approximately 18 months after the onsite assessment.
issues.resolutionHint: Plan to months 15-21 (matches Rule 8 and the T&C definition both); the Rules definitions table (13-24) and the hub approximation (~18 months) are treated as descriptive, not operative.

issues.title: Potency testing cadence wording — per person, drug + dosage-form coverage (confirm with pharmacist manager)
issues.conservativePlanning: Schedule potency tests so each compounding technician AND each compounding pharmacist completes tests on two different drugs and two different dosage forms per year (i.e. per-person drug+form coverage, NOT four combinations of each person; also NOT a single shared program).
issues.requiredShortform: two (2) different drugs × two (2) dosage forms per compounding technician AND per compounding pharmacist per year
issues.shortformNote: requiredShortform is the planning paraphrase; the UAG source wording below does NOT use "(2)" numerals or the "×" sign — keep the verbatim quote in any compliance artefact.

sources.label: UAG V1.1 section 2.4 Key Tasks (verbatim; source of the cadence)
sources.anchorNote: approximate line anchor: pdftotext extraction, lines counted with text.split('\n') (1-indexed); treat as ±20 (clause-index convention); clause-index.md approximates ~3140s, actual location is 3253-3259
sources.quote: Establish a system for final product potency testing to ensure consistency, efficacy and quality. A final product potency test must be completed on two different drugs and two different dosage forms per compounding technician and compounding pharmacist per year.

sources.label: UAG 2.4 evidence examples (records burden)
sources.anchorNote: approximate line anchor: pdftotext extraction, lines counted with text.split('\n') (1-indexed); treat as ±20 (clause-index convention)
sources.quote: Evidence of the pharmacy’s procedure for final product potency testing. / Records of the outcomes from final product potency tests completed.

sources.label: AS85000:2024 clause 2.2.3.8 (the underlying standard wording, no cadence)
sources.anchorNote: approximate line anchor: pdftotext extraction, lines counted with text.split('\n') (1-indexed); treat as ±20 (clause-index convention); clause-index gives 2.2.3.8 @1466 (±20)
sources.quote: 2.2.3.8 The pharmacy shall maintain and follow a system to ensure consistency of compounded products, including appropriate instructions for compounding and a system for final product potency testing.

sources.label: QC2020 5.3.7 (outgoing; per technician only — UAG adds the pharmacist cohort)
sources.anchorNote: approximate line anchor: pdftotext extraction, lines counted with text.split('\n') (1-indexed); treat as ±20 (clause-index convention)
sources.quote: The procedure for ensuring consistency of compounded products including a system for final product potency testing. Documentation of results from final product potency tests completed. A final product potency test must be completed on two different drugs and two different dosage forms per technician per year.

issues.conflict: Not a direct contradiction, but an interpretation: UAG wording "per compounding technician and compounding pharmacist per year" is ambiguous between (a) each person individually covers 2 drugs x 2 dosage forms, and (b) two test programs total (one per technician, one per pharmacist).QC2020 said per technician only.
issues.resolutionHint: Confirm with the pharmacist manager (also flagging readiness-hitlist item 13). Working interpretation: per-person drug+form coverage — each in-scope person does tests on two different drugs and two different dosage forms each year. NOT four combinations of each drug/form pair, NOT a shared single set.
